memory_update.text: MYRG should be tracked as an underfollowed grid-construction and substation-execution candidate for AI data-center interconnection bottlenecks.

POWL should be tracked as a relatively pure electrical-equipment candidate tied to medium-voltage switchgear, power control rooms and data-center electrical packages, though its market cap has moved above the preferred underfollowed range.
BKH should be tracked as a mid-cap regulated utility with unusually explicit Wyoming/Cheyenne data-center load growth, substation agreement and long-lead generation equipment signals.

For AI data-center power, evidence points to multiple bottlenecks: transmission planning, substation capacity, transformer/switchgear availability, utility interconnection queues, regulatory cost allocation and large-load contract execution.

Need a later pass on transformer-specific public suppliers and private-supplier leakage: many named transformer suppliers are private or foreign-listed, so U.S.-listed exposure may be indirect through electrical contractors, switchgear makers, utilities and diversified industrials.

node: Grid interconnection, transmission, substations, utility power procurement and baseload availability
summary: Expanded the universe around the AI data-center power chokepoint with emphasis on underfollowed suppliers and regional regulated assets rather than hyperscalers or mega-cap electrical leaders. The strongest underfollowed candidates in this pass are MYR Group for transmission/substation construction, Powell Industries for medium-voltage switchgear and engineered electrical systems, and Black Hills for concentrated Wyoming/Cheyenne data-center load growth. AEP is included as a reference/regional utility anchor because its large-load pipeline provides evidence that interconnection and take-or-pay utility service agreements are becoming a major AI infrastructure constraint.
